notes: Hindi-only chapter (NCERT Chemistry 12 Ch.1, 'Solutions' - same chapter this repo's own exemplar solutions-chapter-1.html was built from). Much larger/denser than biology-12-1: 13 worked examples, 41 end-of-chapter exercises, and a genuine structural novelty not seen in any prior chapter - 12 'in-text questions' (in NCERT convention, "पाठ्यनिहित प्रश्न") scattered through the chapter body at 4 separate locations, numbered as ONE continuous sequence 1.1-1.12 (not restarting per location), each with a real solved answer in the solutions manual. This is outside step_2/PROMPT.md's literal documented scope (examples + EXERCISES/ADDITIONAL EXERCISES only) and the schema has no dedicated kind for it - asked the user, who decided: tag as kind=additional_exercise with a distinct 'it_' id prefix (it_1.N / sol_it_1.N) rather than 'q_', specifically to avoid colliding with the end-of-chapter exercises' own independent 1.1-1.41 numbering. Given the scale (100K+66K chars, ~1700 inline math spans each in chapter.hi.md and solutions.hi.md), extraction was dispatched to 7 parallel sub-agents per _shared/RULES.md's dispatch guidance (each given only step_2/extract.md, never step_2/PROMPT.md, with an exact bounded line range and exact output scratch path; none touched chapters/ or ran gates/manifest) covering: examples (13), in-text questions (12), in-text solutions (12), exercises split into two halves (20+21), exercise solutions split into two halves (20+21). Every batch's actual output was verified before merging (tag._parse succeeds, exact expected id/count sequence, no duplicates or gaps) rather than trusting each agent's self-report, per RULES.md. Fixed one real gap found during that verification: two solutions (q_1.14 and q_1.37, both about Raoult's-law-deviation graphs) had their referenced figures left as bare inline markdown image syntax inside the solution text rather than proper :::figure blocks - converted both to real :::figure{src=...} blocks (preserving their captions' own OCR artifacts/typos verbatim, not 'fixing' them) so match.join_solutions' figure-merge (the fix already made in pipeline/match.py during biology-12-1's run) actually picks them up. Numerous other agent-caught OCR/LaTeX artifacts (rho used for p/pressure throughout, broken Delta symbols, a stray digit-vs-table-label inconsistency, an apparent genuine textbook duplication in q_1.38's solution) were left exactly as transcribed, per Rule 4/extract.md - none of these are stage 2's to fix; flagging q_1.38's solution (vapour-phase mole fractions for benzene and naphthalene both stated as the identical 0.325, which cannot both be correct) as worth a close look at stage 5 (verify) against the actual solutions PDF page, since it reads like either an OCR line-merge or a genuine manual error rather than an artifact this stage can resolve. join_solutions matched all 12 in-text and all 41 exercise questions to their solutions with 0 needs_review in both cases - not taken on faith given the prior physics-chapter numbering-drift incidents documented in step_2/PROMPT.md: every single question and every single solution was read in full during sub-agent output verification (not sampled), confirming a clean, complete 1:1 mapping on both sides with no NCERT-rationalization gaps.

Hindi-only chapter. Verified all 66 items (13 examples, 41 exercises, 12 in-text questions) against chapter.hi.pdf/solutions.hi.pdf page renders (pymupdf PNGs at 200dpi, since pdftoppm/poppler is unavailable in this environment) via 8 dispatched sub-agents (batches A-H), each given only step_5/verify.md (never step_5/PROMPT.md) with an exact item range and exact scratch output path, per _shared/RULES.md's dispatch-scope rule. First dispatch: 6 of 8 batches hit an HTTP 429 rate limit (reset stated as 2:20pm IST); after the reset time passed, the same 6 batches (C-H) were re-dispatched with identical prompts and all succeeded. 51 corrections returned overall: examples (batches A, B) had zero OCR issues; the overwhelming majority of corrections were in the exercise solutions (batches E-H), dominated by a systematic rho-for-p OCR substitution (Greek rho misread in place of the vapour-pressure symbol p) and assorted single-character Devanagari misreads (dh/gh confusion in dhanaatmak/ghanaatmak, dropped conjuncts). 45 high-confidence corrections applied; 6 medium-confidence corrections held back for manual review rather than auto-applied (per min_confidence='high'), each logged in held with its reason. One coverage gap flagged by batch F (q_1.24's solution falls on sol_27.png, one page past the given sol_21-26 range) was personally checked against sol_27.png after the sub-agent runs - solution text confirmed present and matching, no correction needed, no genuine gap. Three genuine NCERT-source-content discrepancies were found and deliberately left untouched (Rule 4/Rule 5 - not stage 5's call to "fix" the textbook or invent a corrected value): (1) it_1.8's solution computes with a vapour pressure of 700 mm Hg for pure liquid B where the question itself states 750 mm Hg - present in both PDFs as printed; (2) q_1.26's question asks for molarity but the printed solution's own working computes and reports molality: both quantities are internally consistent within their own definitions, only the question/solution vocabulary mismatches, as printed; (3) q_1.38's solution states the vapour-phase mole fraction of both benzene and naphthalene as the identical 0.325, which cannot both be correct simultaneously (they must sum with a third component or to 1) - confirmed present in the solutions PDF's own print, not an OCR/extraction artifact. All three are reported here as known NCERT solutions-manual issues, not pipeline corrections.

Structured via 6 dispatched sub-agents (batches A-F, all 66 items), each given only step_7/format.md + _shared/RULES.md's container-vocabulary section (never step_7/PROMPT.md), working on fully self-contained per-item rendered blocks (render.render_item() output), per _shared/RULES.md's dispatch-scope rule. Roughly 39 of 66 items received genuine inner structure (:::step/:::formula/:::concept/:::table), the rest left as plain paragraph text where the source solution was a single fused derivation or too short to warrant splitting - each batch reported its own item-by-item breakdown of which got structure and why (see prior turns' sub-agent summaries for exact per-item detail; not re-derived here since nothing in structured.hi.md itself records the rationale, only the resulting containers). The fixed Hindi given/key-formula/substitute/conclusion vocabulary (जानकारी/मुख्य सूत्र/मान रखो/निष्कर्ष) was used only where a block genuinely fit that flow; freeform Hindi captions or no label at all were used otherwise, per RULES.md's 'stage 8 infers by position' note. q_1.1's classification table wrapped in :::table (only markdown table in the chapter; q_1.33/q_1.37's own tables also wrapped by batch F); several tempting 'tables' elsewhere were correctly left alone since they are LaTeX aligned math blocks, not markdown tables. No :::part items had a trailing duplicate whole-item solution (none of this chapter's items use :::part at all - confirmed across all 6 batch reports), so that judgement-call scenario never arose here. No figures were moved (q_1.14's two figures and q_1.37's one figure are never explicitly referenced by name in their solution text, so format.md's 'move to first reference point' rule did not apply to any of this chapter's 3 figures). tag._parse succeeds and protect.parity shows zero drift (display math, inline math, tables, images all unchanged in count) between stage 6 and stage 7 text - no wording, digit, symbol or table cell was altered anywhere.

Correction-only follow-up to the earlier format-stage entry, found while preparing stage 8: batch A (examples 1-7) used :::part{label="(i)"}/:::part{label="(ii)"} nested inside ex_1.5s own :::solution block to represent its two calculation stages. :::part is not in step_7/format.mds allowed vocabulary at all (that list is step/formula/table/note/figure/concept only, with an explicit "No other names" rule) - :::part is a stage-4-emitted OUTER container for a genuinely multi-part QUESTION (its own :::prompt/:::solution/:::answer), never something stage 7 adds inside an existing solution. Fixed by replacing both occurrences with :::step{n="1" label="(i)"}/:::step{n="2" label="(ii)"} (same content, same position, correct vocabulary) via direct text substitution - no other line touched. Re-verified both stage 7 gates (tag._parse, protect.parity against 06_simplify) still pass after the fix. No other :::part{ occurrence exists anywhere else in structured.hi.md.

Hindi-only chapter. Serialized via pipeline/serialize.py (pure code, no model call - this stage's only genuine judgment, the given/key_formula/substitute/conclusion inference, was already implemented there as a mechanical rule per step_8/PROMPT.md). Fixed a real bug in serialize.py before running this stage: build_flow() only handled plain text and a bare :::figure, silently dropping any :::concept/:::formula/:::note/:::table nested inside another container - and this chapter's stage 7 output genuinely nests these in 13 places (a :::step wrapping a formula/concept/note/table for narrative flow, and even a :::concept wrapping a :::formula in q_1.3/q_1.12). Added _flatten_children() to promote any such nested block to its own top-level solution_blocks entry, splitting the wrapping block's own text around it (and keeping the wrapper's own kind for the split fragments, so a concept split around a nested formula yields two concept-typed fragments, not step-typed ones). Verified the fix against all 13 flagged cases by comparing whitespace-normalized raw text length vs serialized text length per item - exact match on 8, and the remaining 5 (all in-text-question items: it_1.3, it_1.5, it_1.6, it_1.8, it_1.9) showed only the expected 2-character reduction from stage 8's own documented 'strip a leading हल opener' rule (these items' extracted text genuinely carried a redundant 'हल चरण...' opener inline, confirmed by inspection - not a new drop). Gate passed: item count, part count (0 - this chapter has no :::part-based items), and distinct figure src count all match between the written JSON and a fresh direct count from structured.hi.md. No :::part-based duplicate-solution artifact existed in this chapter (confirmed across all of stage 7's batch reports), so that code path was not exercised here.

Post-hoc corrections from an independent user cross-check against both source PDFs, each confirmed by direct visual inspection before applying (not just trusting the report): (1) it_1.8 (paathyanihit prashna 1.8): chapter.hi.pdf page 15 (a real, direct 200dpi render, not just mathpix OCR) confirms p_B_deg = 750 mm Hg as printed in the actual textbook question. solutions.hi.pdf page 32 (also directly rendered and read) mis-restates the SAME question with 700 mm Hg and carries that through its own working (x_A=0.40 etc) - a genuine textbook-vs-official-solutions-manual discrepancy, not an OCR artifact (both sources internally self-consistent, just disagree with each other). The pipeline's own solution field had silently adopted the solutions-manual's 700 while its own :::prompt already correctly stated 750 - an internal self-contradiction. Corrected to 750 throughout (x_A=0.50, x_B=0.50, y_A=0.375, y_B=0.625), matching the textbook question the item itself is supposed to be solving. (2) it_1.4 (paathyanihit prashna 1.4): chapter.hi.pdf page 5 confirms the question asks for a 0.25 molar, 2.5 kg jaliya vilayan (2.5 kg of SOLUTION, i.e. urea+water) - the existing solution wrongly set the solvent (water) mass to 2.5 kg directly, getting 37.5g. chapter.hi.pdf page 30's own official answer key states '1.4  36.964 g', not 37.5g, confirming the error independently of the user's report. Corrected via proper algebraic setup (water mass = 2500 - W grams), giving 36.95g (matches the textbook's own answer key to within its own printed rounding - exact algebra gives 36.9458g, the textbook prints 36.964g, a ~0.05% difference attributable to the textbook's own rounding, not a new error introduced here). A third reported item (q_1.30, benzoic acid, '0.15 m' treated as 0.15 M with an assumed unstated 250 mL) was investigated and NOT changed: confirmed both chapter.hi.pdf and solutions.hi.pdf treat it the same way (0.15 M + 250 mL assumed) - this is a genuine textbook notation ambiguity (m vs M) that the official solutions manual itself resolved this way, not a transcription error unique to this pipeline. Per Rule 5 (nothing invented) and Rule 1 (the solutions PDF is the source of truth for solution content), the official published resolution was kept as-is rather than substituted with a molality-based re-derivation of my own. Also confirmed as legitimate rounding-only (no action needed): q_1.9 (23.4 vs 23.3806 mm Hg), q_1.10 (121.67 vs 121.7g), q_1.11 (5.077 vs 5.0769g) - all verified against chapter.hi.pdf page 30's own answer key, all consistent.

Verified 66/66 items parse cleanly after the edit.

ONE STRUCTURAL SUBTLETY CAUGHT: it_1.8's :::concept{label="जानकारी"} sits nested inside its own :::step{n="1"} in 07_format/structured.hi.md (pre-existing nesting, not introduced by this fix) - a fresh generic re-parse flattens the concept's content into the parent step's own flow, collapsing 4 solution_blocks down to 2 and silently losing the item's separate जानकारी pill on the rendered page. Instead, directly hand-edited the two affected regions of the already-published 09_design/final.hi.html, matching the exact existing HTML conventions (s23/s24/s26/s27 pill/line classes, s31/s32/s33 nested fraction spans, plain (non-nbsp) spaces, as already used throughout this file) rather than reconstructing an unknown-fidelity new script. it_1.4's जानकारी pill gained a new sentence explaining the solution-mass-vs-solvent-mass distinction (with a small nested fraction for (2500-W)/1000), its मान रखो pill rewritten with the 4-line algebraic solve, and its निष्कर्ष box changed from '37.5 g' to '≈ 36.95 g'. it_1.8's जानकारी/मान रखो/निष्कर्ष pills had only their numbers changed (700->750 mm Hg cascading through x_A/x_B/p_A/p_B/y_A/y_B).
